edges.relation: Acceptance test drives the implemented endpoint
Acceptance test drives the implemented browser search layer

nodes.name: server-users
nodes.task: Implement the users search endpoint in server/users.ts against the existing immutable contract in contracts/users.json (treat it as the sole authoritative source for request parameters, response shape, error payloads and pagination fields). Requirements: `q` filtering over the contract's searchable user fields; cursor-based pagination using the contract's cursor/page-size/next-cursor semantics; the exact 400 error for an invalid/malformed cursor and the exact 500 error for internal failure as specified by the contract. Do not modify contracts/users.json or any package manifest. Add server-side unit tests (alongside the existing server test conventions) covering: q filtering, first page and subsequent page navigation via cursor, invalid cursor returning the 400 shape, and the 500 error path (forced failure). Completion evidence: the endpoint module and its unit tests exist and the tests pass.

nodes.name: web-users
nodes.task: Implement the users search client/UI layer in web/users.ts against the existing immutable contract in contracts/users.json (authoritative for request parameters, response shape, cursor pagination fields and error payloads). Requirements: debounced search input; cursor pagination (load-next using the cursor returned by the previous response); explicit loading, empty and error states; and protection against stale/out-of-order responses so an older in-flight request can never overwrite newer results or UI state (e.g. request sequence/token or abort-based superseding). Keep the public interface usable by browser tests hitting the real endpoint shape. Do not modify contracts/users.json or any package manifest. Add browser unit tests covering: debounce behaviour (intermediate queries not sent or superseded), loading state, empty results, error state for 400/500 responses, pagination advancing via returned cursor, and a deliberately out-of-order response pair where the earlier request resolves last. Completion evidence: web/users.ts and its browser unit tests exist and the tests pass.

nodes.name: users-flow-acceptance
nodes.task: Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts that runs the browser-side users search (web/users.ts) against the real users search endpoint (server/users.ts), using contracts/users.json as the authoritative request/response/error shape. Exercise at minimum: an end-to-end q filter returning matching users; cursor pagination across successive pages from the browser through the endpoint; the 400 invalid-cursor path (browser surfaces the error state when the endpoint rejects a bad cursor); the 500 path; and an out-of-order/stale-response scenario verified against the live endpoint (earlier request resolves after a newer one and must not overwrite the newer results or cursor state). Do not modify contracts/users.json, any package manifest, or weaken either module's behaviour to make tests pass — if a defect is exposed in server/users.ts or web/users.ts, report the exact failing assertion, the file and the required correction rather than adapting the contract or assertions. Completion evidence: tests/users-flow.test.ts exists, runs the browser against the endpoint, passes, and the plan's untouched-file constraint (contract and package manifest byte-identical to their original state) is confirmed.

originalGoal: Deliver users search using the existing immutable contracts/users.json contract. Implement server/users.ts with q filtering, cursor pagination and the specified 400/500 errors, and server unit tests. Implement web/users.ts with debounced search, pagination, loading/empty/error states and protection against stale responses, with browser unit tests. Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts exercising the browser against the endpoint, including invalid cursors and out-of-order responses. Keep the published contract and package manifest unchanged.
